passages.title: City Unveils 14-Kilometre Cycle Network on Its Busiest Roads
paragraphs: A mid-sized city in north-eastern Thailand last week opened its first network of protected cycle lanes, physically separating bicycles from motor traffic with a raised concrete kerb along 14 kilometres of its busiest roads. Municipal officials say the 60-million-baht scheme is designed to make cycling feel safe not only for confident commuters but also for schoolchildren, older residents and first-time riders.

The project was prompted by a two-year review of local accident records, which found that cyclists and pedestrians accounted for nearly a third of road deaths in the city, even though they made up only about one in ten trips. Supporters also highlight the public health benefits of regular cycling, including lower rates of obesity and heart disease, and argue that fewer cars would reduce residents' exposure to exhaust fumes in congested districts.

Not everyone, however, is convinced. Shop owners along the central market road complain that the new lanes have eliminated around 200 roadside parking spaces, and they fear that customers who usually arrive by car will simply shop elsewhere. “Most of our buyers do not come on bicycles,” said one fabric seller, who asked not to be named.

City planners acknowledge that such worries are understandable but suggest they may prove unfounded, noting that similar schemes abroad have often increased the number of shoppers passing by. They will monitor sales and traffic flows for twelve months and have promised to create short-stay parking on side streets if trade declines significantly.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Cycling has overtaken driving as the most common way of travelling around the city.
A city has built separated cycle lanes for safety and health reasons, though some traders object.
Shop owners have persuaded city officials to remove part of a newly opened network of cycle lanes.
Road deaths among cyclists have fallen sharply since the city opened its new network of lanes.
questions.explain: ข่าวนี้มีสองด้าน: ¶1–2 อธิบายเลนจักรยานที่สร้างขึ้นเพื่อความปลอดภัยและสุขภาพ ส่วน ¶3 เปิดด้วย “Not everyone, however, is convinced.” เพื่อนำเสนอเสียงคัดค้านของเจ้าของร้าน ตัวเลือก D ผิดเพราะเลนเพิ่งเปิดเมื่อสัปดาห์ก่อน ยังไม่มีข้อมูลว่าการเสียชีวิตลดลง และ C ผิดเพราะเมืองยังไม่ได้รื้อเลนใดเลย

questions.q: According to paragraph 1, what makes the new cycle lanes 'protected'?
options: They are closed to all motor vehicles during school hours.
They are watched by traffic cameras along their entire length.
They are painted in a colour that drivers can see easily.
They are kept apart from cars by a raised concrete kerb.
questions.explain: ¶1: “physically separating bicycles from motor traffic with a raised concrete kerb” — สิ่งที่ทำให้เลนได้ชื่อว่า protected คือขอบคอนกรีตยกสูงที่กั้นจากรถยนต์ ตัวเลือก A เป็นกับดักเพราะย่อหน้าเดียวกันพูดถึง schoolchildren แต่ไม่มีการปิดถนนช่วงเวลาเรียน

questions.q: It can be inferred from paragraph 2 that cyclists and pedestrians in the city
options: are killed far more often than their share of trips would suggest
are to blame for about a third of all serious road accidents in the city
make up roughly thirty per cent of all the journeys made in the city each day
are mostly schoolchildren and older residents who are unable to drive
questions.explain: ¶2: กลุ่มนี้คิดเป็น “nearly a third of road deaths … even though they made up only about one in ten trips” แปลว่าเสี่ยงตายสูงเกินสัดส่วนการเดินทางของตนมาก ตัวเลือก C สลับตัวเลข (หนึ่งในสามคือสัดส่วนผู้เสียชีวิต ไม่ใช่การเดินทาง) ส่วน B ผิดเพราะข่าวไม่ได้ระบุว่าใครเป็นฝ่ายก่ออุบัติเหตุ

questions.q: The word 'congested' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: heavily polluted
mainly residential
full of traffic
poorly designed
questions.explain: ‘congested’ = แออัด/การจราจรหนาแน่น ¶2: “reduce residents' exposure to exhaust fumes in congested districts” หมายถึงย่านที่มีรถมาก ตัวเลือก A เป็นกับดักเพราะในประโยคมีคำว่า exhaust fumes แต่มลพิษเป็นผลของรถติด ไม่ใช่ความหมายของคำนี้

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a benefit of the cycling scheme?
options: safer conditions for less experienced riders
more tourists visiting the city
lower rates of obesity and heart disease
less exposure to fumes from vehicles
questions.explain: ประโยชน์ที่ข่าวกล่าวถึงคือความปลอดภัยของ “first-time riders” (¶1) รวมทั้งโรคอ้วน โรคหัวใจ และควันไอเสีย (¶2) แต่ไม่มีตอนใดพูดถึงนักท่องเที่ยวเลย จึงตอบ B

questions.q: The word 'they' in paragraph 3 refers to
options: shop owners
the new lanes
customers
parking spaces
questions.explain: ¶3: “Shop owners … complain … and they fear that customers … will simply shop elsewhere” — ผู้ที่ ‘กลัว’ คือเจ้าของร้าน ตัวเลือก C ผิดเพราะลูกค้าคือสิ่งที่เจ้าของร้านกังวลว่าจะหายไป ไม่ใช่ผู้กังวลเอง

questions.q: The word 'unfounded' in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to
options: not yet officially recorded
not shared by most residents
not based on real evidence
not possible to measure accurately
questions.explain: ‘unfounded’ = ไม่มีมูล/ไม่มีหลักฐานรองรับ ¶4: planners “suggest they may prove unfounded, noting that similar schemes abroad have often increased the number of shoppers” คือยกหลักฐานจากต่างประเทศมาแย้งว่าความกลัวอาจไม่เป็นจริง ตัวเลือก B ผิดเพราะประเด็นไม่ใช่จำนวนคนที่เห็นด้วย

questions.q: The city planners' attitude toward the shop owners' worries can best be described as
options: dismissive and openly hostile
alarmed and deeply apologetic
completely indifferent
sympathetic but unconvinced
questions.explain: ¶4: นักวางผังเมือง “acknowledge that such worries are understandable” (เห็นใจ) แต่มองว่าอาจ “prove unfounded” (ไม่คล้อยตาม) และยังสัญญาว่าจะเพิ่มที่จอดรถหากยอดขายตก ท่าทีที่ยอมรับฟังเช่นนี้จึงไม่ใช่การเพิกเฉย (C) หรือเป็นปฏิปักษ์ (A)

passages.title: Graduate Research Scholarships 2027
paragraphs: The Graduate School invites applications for its 2027 Graduate Research Scholarships, which support master's and doctoral research addressing health, environmental or social challenges in the Mekong region. Up to fifteen awards will be made this year.

Eligibility: Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a graduate programme at the university, and their research proposal must have been approved by their programme committee before the closing date. Students in their final semester, as well as those already holding a full scholarship from another source, are not eligible. Applicants need not be Thai nationals.

Value: Master's students will receive 120,000 baht and doctoral students 250,000 baht, paid in two instalments: 60 per cent upon signing the award agreement and the remainder once a satisfactory progress report has been accepted. Funds may cover fieldwork, laboratory materials and conference travel, but not tuition fees or personal equipment such as laptops.

Required documents: A complete application comprises (1) the online application form, (2) a research proposal of no more than ten pages, (3) an official transcript and (4) a letter of support from the principal supervisor. Evidence of English proficiency is required only where the project involves an overseas partner institution.

Deadline and selection: Applications close at 4:30 p.m. on 15 January 2027; late or incomplete submissions will not be considered. A panel of senior academics will shortlist candidates on the basis of academic merit and the potential impact of the proposed research. Shortlisted applicants will be invited to a fifteen-minute interview in late February, and results will be announced by 31 March. Enquiries should be directed to the Graduate School's research office.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of this announcement?
options: to report the results of last year's scholarship competition
to explain how programme committees approve research proposals
to invite eligible students to apply for research funding
to announce new rules for students who already hold scholarships
questions.explain: ¶1: “The Graduate School invites applications for its 2027 Graduate Research Scholarships” — ประกาศนี้มีไว้เชิญชวนให้สมัครทุน ตัวเลือก A ผิดเพราะผลการคัดเลือกยังไม่ออก (จะประกาศภายใน 31 มีนาคม) ส่วน D ผิดเพราะผู้ถือทุนอยู่แล้วถูกกล่าวถึงเพียงในฐานะผู้ที่ไม่มีสิทธิ์สมัคร

questions.q: The word 'those' in paragraph 2 refers to
options: students
proposals
scholarships
committees
questions.explain: ¶2: “Students in their final semester, as well as those already holding a full scholarship from another source, are not eligible” — ‘those’ คือนักศึกษาที่ถือทุนเต็มจำนวนอยู่แล้ว ตัวเลือก C เป็นกับดักเพราะ scholarship คือสิ่งที่คนกลุ่มนี้ถือครอง ไม่ใช่สิ่งที่ ‘those’ ใช้แทน

questions.q: Based on the eligibility rules, which of the following students could apply?
options: a part-time master's student whose proposal was approved last year
a doctoral student from Laos studying full-time with an approved proposal
a full-time master's student who will graduate at the end of this semester
a full-time doctoral student who is fully funded by a government scholarship
questions.explain: ¶2 ระบุว่า “Applicants need not be Thai nationals” นักศึกษาลาวที่เรียนเต็มเวลาและโครงร่างผ่านการอนุมัติแล้วจึงสมัครได้ ตัวเลือก A เรียนไม่เต็มเวลา, C กำลังเรียนภาคเรียนสุดท้าย และ D มีทุนเต็มจำนวนจากแหล่งอื่นแล้ว ทั้งสามจึงขาดคุณสมบัติ

questions.q: How much will a doctoral student receive when the award agreement is signed?
options: 72,000 baht
questions.explain: ¶3: นักศึกษาปริญญาเอกได้ 250,000 บาท และงวดแรกจ่าย “60 per cent upon signing the award agreement” = 150,000 บาท ตัวเลือก A คือ 60% ของทุนปริญญาโท ส่วน B คือเงินงวดที่สอง (40%) ของปริญญาเอก

questions.q: The word 'remainder' in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
options: the rest of the money
an extra bonus payment
a written reminder
a refund of fees
questions.explain: ‘remainder’ = ส่วนที่เหลือ ¶3: “60 per cent upon signing … and the remainder once a satisfactory progress report has been accepted” คือเงินอีก 40% ที่ยังไม่ได้จ่าย ตัวเลือก C เป็นกับดักการสะกด เพราะ reminder (สิ่งเตือนความจำ) หน้าตาคล้าย remainder แต่ความหมายต่างกันโดยสิ้นเชิง

questions.q: Which of the following could NOT be paid for with scholarship funds?
options: travel to present a paper at a conference
chemicals needed for laboratory experiments
a laptop for writing up the thesis
transport costs during fieldwork
questions.explain: ¶3: “… but not tuition fees or personal equipment such as laptops” แล็ปท็อปจึงเบิกไม่ได้ ส่วน A, B และ D ตรงกับ conference travel, laboratory materials และ fieldwork ที่ประกาศอนุญาตไว้

questions.q: According to the announcement, which document must be submitted by only some applicants?
options: an official academic transcript
proof of English proficiency
a letter from the principal supervisor
a research proposal of up to ten pages
questions.explain: ¶4: “Evidence of English proficiency is required only where the project involves an overseas partner institution.” จึงยื่นเฉพาะโครงการที่มีสถาบันคู่ร่วมมือในต่างประเทศ ส่วนเอกสารในตัวเลือกอื่นอยู่ในรายการ (1)–(4) ที่ผู้สมัครทุกคนต้องยื่น

questions.q: According to paragraph 5, how will candidates be shortlisted?
options: by how well they perform in a fifteen-minute interview
by the date and time at which they submit their applications
by recommendations from the Graduate School's research office
by academic merit and the likely impact of their research
questions.explain: ¶5: “A panel of senior academics will shortlist candidates on the basis of academic merit and the potential impact of the proposed research.” ตัวเลือก A ผิดเพราะการสัมภาษณ์มีขึ้นหลังจากผ่านเข้ารอบแล้ว ส่วน C ผิดเพราะสำนักงานวิจัยมีหน้าที่เพียงตอบข้อสงสัย

passages.title: Pharmacists Welcome Plan as Survey Finds Metals in Supplements
paragraphs: Herbal medicines and dietary supplements will face considerably stricter controls under draft rules published this week by a national medicines regulator in Southeast Asia. If adopted, the rules would oblige manufacturers to demonstrate that their products meet basic quality standards before they reach pharmacy shelves, rather than after problems have been reported.

At present, most such products are registered on the basis of documents supplied by the manufacturers themselves, and only a small fraction are ever tested independently. Officials admit that this system has allowed substandard products to circulate for months before being withdrawn. In a recent market survey of 300 supplements carried out by a university laboratory, roughly one sample in eight contained heavy metals such as lead or arsenic above permitted limits, while several “natural” slimming capsules were found to contain prescription drugs that were not declared on the label.

Labelling is a second target. Under the proposals, packaging would have to list every active ingredient together with its quantity, and claims that a product can “cure” or “prevent” a disease would be prohibited unless backed by clinical evidence. Products would also have to carry warnings about possible interactions with conventional medicines; St John's wort, for instance, can reduce the effectiveness of some blood thinners and contraceptive pills.

Pharmacists have broadly welcomed the plan. “Patients often assume that anything herbal is harmless, so many never mention to their doctor what they are taking,” said Dr. Nattaya Sombat, a hospital pharmacist. “Clearer labels would make those conversations much easier and, frankly, safer.”

Some producers of traditional remedies, however, warn that the cost of laboratory testing could drive small family businesses out of the market. “Our recipes have been trusted for generations, and they deserve different treatment from factory-made chemicals,” said the owner of one such business. In response to these concerns, regulators have proposed a three-year transition period and subsidised testing for small manufacturers.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Herbal medicines are generally more dangerous than conventional prescription drugs.
Draft rules would require tighter quality checks and fuller labels for herbal products.
Small producers of traditional remedies are being forced out of business by testing costs.
Pharmacists have found that many slimming supplements contain hidden prescription drugs.
questions.explain: ¶1 ให้ใจความหลักว่าผลิตภัณฑ์สมุนไพรและอาหารเสริม “will face considerably stricter controls under draft rules” แล้ว ¶2–3 ขยายเรื่องการตรวจคุณภาพและฉลาก ตัวเลือก D เป็นกับดักจากชื่อข่าว เพราะผลสำรวจใน ¶2 มาจากห้องปฏิบัติการของมหาวิทยาลัย ไม่ใช่เภสัชกร และเป็นเพียงรายละเอียดสนับสนุน

questions.q: According to paragraph 2, how are most herbal products currently registered?
options: after independent testing in a university laboratory
after a review of complaints received from patients
on the basis of clinical trials approved by pharmacists
on the basis of documents supplied by the manufacturers
questions.explain: ¶2: “most such products are registered on the basis of documents supplied by the manufacturers themselves” ตัวเลือก A เป็นกับดักคำ เพราะห้องแล็บของมหาวิทยาลัยทำเพียงการสำรวจตลาด และข่าวระบุว่ามีเพียง “a small fraction” เท่านั้นที่ถูกตรวจโดยอิสระ

questions.q: The word 'circulate' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: be withdrawn from shops
be passed around and sold
be checked again and again
be manufactured cheaply
questions.explain: ‘circulate’ = แพร่กระจาย/หมุนเวียนวางขายในตลาด ¶2: “this system has allowed substandard products to circulate for months before being withdrawn” — ถ้าแปลว่า withdrawn (A) จะขัดกับวลี before being withdrawn ในประโยคเดียวกันทันที

questions.q: According to the survey described in paragraph 2, some slimming capsules
options: contained higher levels of lead than any other product tested
had been wrongly registered as prescription medicines
contained medicines that were not listed on the label
had been withdrawn from sale before the survey began
questions.explain: ¶2: slimming capsules “were found to contain prescription drugs that were not declared on the label” ตัวเลือก A ผิดเพราะข่าวไม่ได้เปรียบเทียบปริมาณตะกั่วระหว่างผลิตภัณฑ์ และโลหะหนักพบในตัวอย่างราวหนึ่งในแปดโดยรวม ไม่ได้เจาะจงที่แคปซูลลดน้ำหนัก

questions.q: It can be inferred from paragraph 3 that, at present, some product labels
options: claim to cure diseases without clinical evidence
already warn about interactions with other medicines
list too many ingredients for patients to understand
are checked by pharmacists before the products are sold
questions.explain: ¶3: claims to “cure” or “prevent” a disease “would be prohibited unless backed by clinical evidence” — การต้องออกกฎห้ามแสดงว่าปัจจุบันยังมีฉลากที่อ้างเช่นนั้นโดยไม่มีหลักฐาน ตัวเลือก B ผิดเพราะคำว่า “would also have to carry warnings” บ่งว่าคำเตือนเรื่องปฏิกิริยาระหว่างยายังไม่ใช่ข้อบังคับในตอนนี้

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a labelling requirement under the proposals?
options: stating the amount of each active ingredient
warning about interactions with other medicines
having clinical evidence for any claim to cure a disease
naming the country where the product was made
questions.explain: ¶3 ระบุข้อกำหนดสามข้อ ได้แก่ “list every active ingredient together with its quantity”, ห้ามอ้างรักษาโรคหากไม่มี clinical evidence และต้องมีคำเตือนเรื่อง interactions แต่ไม่มีการกล่าวถึงประเทศผู้ผลิต จึงตอบ D

questions.q: The phrase 'those conversations' in paragraph 4 refers to discussions between
options: regulators and manufacturers about the cost of testing
patients and doctors about the products patients take
pharmacists and regulators about the design of labels
small producers and their customers about safety
questions.explain: ก่อนหน้านั้นใน ¶4 Dr. Nattaya กล่าวว่า “many never mention to their doctor what they are taking” ดังนั้น ‘those conversations’ คือการพูดคุยระหว่างผู้ป่วยกับแพทย์เรื่องผลิตภัณฑ์ที่ใช้อยู่ ตัวเลือก C เป็นกับดักเพราะผู้พูดเป็นเภสัชกรและพูดถึงฉลาก แต่ไม่ได้หมายถึงการหารือกับหน่วยงานกำกับ

questions.q: Which of the following statements is an opinion rather than a fact?
options: A university laboratory tested 300 supplements in a recent survey.
Regulators have proposed a three-year transition period for small firms.
Traditional recipes deserve different treatment from factory chemicals.
The draft rules were published this week by a national medicines regulator.
questions.explain: ¶5: เจ้าของกิจการกล่าวว่าสูตรยาของตน “deserve different treatment from factory-made chemicals” ซึ่งเป็นการตัดสินเชิงคุณค่าที่พิสูจน์ไม่ได้ ขณะที่ A, B และ D เป็นเหตุการณ์ที่ตรวจสอบได้ (การสำรวจ 300 ตัวอย่าง ระยะเปลี่ยนผ่านสามปี และการเผยแพร่ร่างกฎ)

questions.q: What is the purpose of paragraph 5?
options: to present an objection to the plan and the regulators' response
to show that traditional remedies are safer than imported supplements
to explain why the draft rules are unlikely to be adopted
to argue that small manufacturers should be exempt from testing
questions.explain: ¶5 เริ่มด้วยข้อคัดค้านว่าค่าตรวจ “could drive small family businesses out of the market” แล้วปิดด้วยมาตรการตอบสนองของหน่วยงาน คือระยะเปลี่ยนผ่านสามปีและเงินอุดหนุนค่าตรวจ ตัวเลือก D ผิดเพราะหน่วยงานไม่ได้ยกเว้นการตรวจ เพียงช่วยแบ่งเบาภาระ

passages.title: Home, Office or Somewhere in Between?
paragraphs: When offices emptied during the COVID-19 pandemic, many managers predicted that productivity would collapse. Several years on, the evidence paints a far more complicated picture — one in which the answer depends on the type of work involved, the way remote arrangements are designed and how productivity is measured in the first place.

Some of the most encouraging findings come from studies of routine tasks whose output is easy to count. In one experiment at an insurance company, staff who processed claims from home completed about 8 per cent more cases per week than colleagues who remained in the office. The researchers attributed much of the gain to fewer interruptions and to the time saved on commuting, which some employees reinvested in their work.

Research on collaborative and creative work, by contrast, has produced less flattering results. An analysis of messaging data from several thousand employees at a software firm found that, once the company went fully remote, staff communicated mainly with their immediate teammates and far less with colleagues in other departments. Because new ideas often emerge from such informal contact across groups, the researchers warned that the damage might take years to become visible — long after short-term output figures had been reported.

Hybrid models, in which employees spend two or three days a week in the office, are increasingly presented as a compromise. A 2024 survey of 2,000 employees at mid-sized firms in Thailand and Malaysia found that hybrid workers reported higher job satisfaction than either fully remote or fully office-based staff, and that they were noticeably less likely to plan to leave their jobs. Managers' ratings of their performance, meanwhile, showed no significant difference.

Measurement itself remains a major obstacle. In many professional jobs, output cannot be reduced to a single number, so managers tend to rely on what they can observe — who arrives early and who stays late. Remote employees may therefore be judged less favourably even when they accomplish just as much. Conversely, employees' own estimates of their productivity are often more generous than those of their supervisors, and longer working hours at home can mean that total output rises while output per hour falls.

“Asking whether remote work is good or bad for productivity is like asking whether meetings are good or bad,” says Dr. Kanokwan Prasert, a labour economist. “The real question is which tasks, which people and which kind of arrangement.”

questions.q: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
options: Remote Work Has Failed, Managers Conclude
Why Hybrid Work Has Become the Global Standard
Remote Work and Productivity: No Simple Answer
How Long Commutes Are Damaging Employee Health

passages.title: Beyond the Clinic: Noncommunicable Diseases and National Development
paragraphs: For much of the twentieth century, heart disease, cancer, diabetes and chronic lung disease were regarded as the price of prosperity — conditions that afflicted the elderly populations of wealthy nations once infectious diseases had been brought under control. That view is now badly outdated. Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) have become the leading cause of death worldwide, and their burden is growing fastest in low- and middle-income countries, many of which are still struggling with tuberculosis, malaria and other infections. This article argues that NCDs should be understood not only as a medical problem but as an economic one, and that money spent on preventing them is better described as an investment than as a cost.

The scale of the problem is difficult to overstate. NCDs account for roughly seven in every ten deaths globally, and a substantial proportion of these are classified as premature, meaning that they occur before the age of 70. Contrary to the old stereotype, most premature NCD deaths now occur in low- and middle-income countries, where populations are ageing rapidly and where diets, working patterns and levels of physical activity have changed dramatically within a single generation. Epidemiologists describe the long-term shift from a pattern of illness dominated by infections to one dominated by chronic conditions as the epidemiological transition. In many countries, however, this transition remains incomplete, so health systems must cope with both burdens at once.

The most direct economic consequence is lost productivity. When a factory supervisor dies of a stroke at 52, or a teacher retires early because of kidney failure, the economy loses not only their current output but also skills and experience accumulated over decades. Illness also reduces the productivity of those who remain in work. Absenteeism — days taken off because of sickness or medical appointments — is relatively easy to record. Harder to detect, but often more costly, is presenteeism: the loss of output that occurs when employees come to work but perform below their normal capacity because of pain, fatigue or the side effects of treatment. A study of manufacturing workers in Southeast Asia, for example, estimated that presenteeism linked to poorly controlled diabetes cost employers almost twice as much as the sick days associated with the same condition.

For households, the burden is felt more immediately. Unlike an acute infection, which is typically treated within days or weeks, a chronic condition may require medication, monitoring and specialist care for the rest of a patient's life. Where health insurance is limited, these recurring expenses are paid largely out of pocket. Health economists use the term catastrophic health expenditure to describe spending that exceeds a set share of a household's capacity to pay, commonly 40 per cent of the income remaining after basic needs such as food have been met. Families facing such costs often resort to borrowing at high interest, selling land or livestock, or withdrawing children from school — choices that can trap them in poverty long after the patient has recovered or died. Moreover, the unpaid work of caring for a chronically ill relative falls disproportionately on women, many of whom reduce their working hours or leave paid employment altogether.

When these individual and household losses are added together, the macroeconomic picture becomes alarming. Chronic illness shrinks the labour force, reduces the savings that households would otherwise invest, and diverts public money from education and infrastructure towards long-term treatment. Modelling studies suggest that, over two decades, the cumulative output lost to the major NCDs in a typical middle-income economy could amount to a substantial fraction of a full year's gross domestic product. Countries with rapidly ageing populations, such as Thailand, are particularly exposed, because they will have proportionally fewer workers to support a growing number of people who need long-term care.

Against this background, prevention appears remarkably inexpensive. Many of the most effective measures operate at the level of the whole population rather than the individual patient: raising taxes on tobacco, alcohol and sugar-sweetened beverages; reducing the salt content of processed foods; restricting the marketing of unhealthy products to children; and designing cities in which walking and cycling are safe and convenient. Such policies cost governments relatively little to implement, and taxes actually generate revenue. One modelling exercise covering several Asian countries estimated that every dollar invested in a package of such measures could yield between five and ten dollars in economic benefits over fifteen years, largely through longer and healthier working lives.

Why, then, do governments continue to underinvest in prevention? Part of the explanation lies in the nature of the benefits themselves. A heart attack that never happens does not appear in any hospital record, and the savings it represents are spread across many years and many budgets. Political leaders, by contrast, are judged on visible achievements within short electoral cycles, and a new hospital wing is far easier to celebrate than a gradual decline in average blood pressure. Industries whose profits depend on tobacco, alcohol or processed food also lobby vigorously against regulation. Finally, ministries of finance have traditionally classified health spending as consumption rather than investment, so prevention competes for funds with every other form of current expenditure.

Overcoming these obstacles will require a change in the way NCDs are framed and measured. If governments routinely calculated the long-term returns of prevention — in productivity, tax revenue and avoided household poverty — the case for action would become far harder to ignore. Health ministries cannot achieve this alone; agriculture, trade, transport and education policies all shape the conditions in which chronic diseases develop. Treating NCD prevention as a shared, cross-government investment rather than as a narrow health expense may therefore be the most important step that countries can take to protect both the well-being of their citizens and the prosperity of their economies.

passages.title: Southeast Asia at an Energy Crossroads: Renewables in a Fast-Growing Region
paragraphs: Few regions illustrate the dilemmas of the global energy transition as clearly as Southeast Asia. Rising incomes, urbanisation and industrial growth have made it one of the fastest-growing sources of electricity demand in the world, and most of that demand is still met by burning coal and natural gas. At the same time, the region is exceptionally vulnerable to climate change, from rising seas in its crowded river deltas to stronger tropical storms. It also possesses abundant renewable resources: strong sunshine throughout the year, promising offshore wind sites and, in some countries, considerable geothermal and hydropower potential. This article argues that the main barriers to a faster transition are no longer technological but institutional — they lie in grids, finance and the fair distribution of costs and benefits.

Solar power offers the clearest evidence of what is possible. The cost of solar panels has fallen dramatically over the past decade, making new solar farms competitive with new fossil-fuel plants in many locations. Vietnam provides a striking example. After the government introduced generous feed-in tariffs — guaranteed prices paid for every unit of electricity fed into the grid — investors installed well over ten gigawatts of solar capacity within roughly two years, transforming a country with almost no solar power into a regional leader. Yet the boom also exposed a serious weakness. Transmission lines in the sunniest provinces could not carry all the electricity being produced, and grid operators were forced to order curtailment, instructing plants to reduce output even when the sun was shining. For investors who had expected to sell every kilowatt-hour, the losses were considerable.

Wind power presents a more mixed picture. Average wind speeds over much of the region's land are low, limiting onshore turbines to a few favourable areas. Offshore, however, conditions are considerably better, particularly along the coasts of Vietnam and the Philippines, where steady monsoon winds blow across wide, shallow continental shelves. Developing these sites is nonetheless far from straightforward. Turbines must be engineered to survive typhoons, specialised ports and vessels are needed for installation, and projects often take close to a decade to move from initial surveys to operation.

Whatever the mix of technologies, a power system that relies heavily on sun and wind must be able to cope with variability. Solar output disappears every evening, just as household demand peaks, and wind output can fall for days at a time. Most of the region's grids, however, were designed to distribute electricity from a small number of large, centralised power stations, not to balance thousands of small and intermittent generators. Three responses are commonly proposed. The first is to strengthen and digitise national grids so that electricity can be moved quickly from where it is generated to where it is needed. The second is cross-border interconnection: regional planners have long promoted an integrated ASEAN Power Grid, and some trade already takes place, with hydropower from Laos, for instance, exported to neighbouring countries. The third is storage, whether in large battery installations, which have become much cheaper recently, or in pumped hydro schemes that use surplus electricity to pump water uphill for release when demand rises.

Even where the technical solutions are clear, paying for them is not. Renewable projects are capital-intensive: almost all of their costs are incurred at the start, during construction, whereas the sunlight and wind they use are free. This makes them unusually sensitive to the cost of capital — the interest rates and returns that lenders and investors demand. In many developing economies, perceived risks such as currency fluctuations, uncertain regulation and the weak finances of state-owned utilities push this cost to two or three times the level in wealthy countries. As a result, an identical solar farm may produce considerably more expensive electricity in Manila or Jakarta than in Madrid. International initiatives such as the Just Energy Transition Partnerships agreed with Indonesia and Vietnam in 2022 aim to lower these costs by blending public and private money, although critics note that much of the promised funding consists of loans rather than grants.

A further complication is the region's existing fleet of coal-fired power stations. Unlike those in Europe or North America, many of these plants are less than fifteen years old and were financed on the assumption that they would operate for thirty or forty years. Many also operate under long-term contracts that oblige utilities to pay for their electricity whether or not it is needed. Retiring the plants early would turn them into stranded assets — investments that lose their value before the end of their expected lifetimes — and someone, whether owners, governments or consumers, would have to absorb the losses. Several proposed schemes would use low-cost international finance to buy out such plants and close them early, but the sums involved are large and the negotiations politically sensitive.

Finally, the transition must be fair if it is to be politically sustainable — the principle commonly described as a just transition. Coal-mining districts in Indonesia, for example, depend heavily on the industry for jobs and local government revenue, and closing mines without credible alternatives would provoke strong resistance. Renewable projects can create injustices of their own: large solar farms and hydropower dams require land, and communities that are displaced or lose access to rivers and forests rarely share in the benefits. Meaningful consultation, retraining for workers and protection for poorer households against sharp rises in electricity prices are therefore not optional extras but conditions for success.

Southeast Asia's energy future is not yet fixed. The falling cost of clean technologies gives the region a genuine opportunity to meet its growing demand without locking itself into decades of fossil-fuel dependence. Whether it seizes that opportunity will depend less on engineering breakthroughs than on decisions about grid investment, financial risk and the sharing of burdens — decisions that are, in the end, political.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Vietnam's rapid solar expansion offers a model that other countries should simply copy.
Coal will remain the region's main source of power because renewables are too unreliable.
The main barriers to the region's clean-energy shift are now institutional, not technical.
Offshore wind is the most promising energy source in the region despite its long lead times.
questions.explain: ¶1 ประกาศจุดยืนว่า “the main barriers to a faster transition are no longer technological but institutional” และ ¶8 ย้ำว่าผลลัพธ์ขึ้นกับการตัดสินใจเรื่องระบบสายส่ง ความเสี่ยงทางการเงิน และการแบ่งภาระ ตัวเลือก A ผิดเพราะ ¶2 ชี้ว่าการขยายตัวของเวียดนามเผยจุดอ่อนของระบบสายส่ง ส่วน D เป็นเพียงรายละเอียดใน ¶3

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in paragraph 1 as a renewable resource found in Southeast Asia?
options: year-round sunshine
offshore wind
geothermal heat
tidal power
questions.explain: ¶1 ระบุทรัพยากรไว้ว่า “strong sunshine throughout the year, promising offshore wind sites and, in some countries, considerable geothermal and hydropower potential” ไม่มีพลังงานจากน้ำขึ้นน้ำลง (tidal) จึงตอบ D

questions.q: The word 'exposed' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: caused
revealed
repaired
concealed
questions.explain: ‘exposed’ = เผยให้เห็น ¶2: “Yet the boom also exposed a serious weakness.” ประโยคถัดมาอธิบายว่าสายส่งรับไฟฟ้าไม่ไหว ตัวเลือก A (caused) เป็นกับดัก เพราะข้อจำกัดของสายส่งมีอยู่ก่อนแล้ว การเติบโตของโซลาร์เพียงทำให้ปัญหาปรากฏออกมา

questions.q: It can be inferred from paragraph 2 that in Vietnam
options: solar capacity grew faster than the transmission network was expanded
the government stopped guaranteeing prices because panels became too costly
solar investors earned larger profits than they had originally expected
plants were told to cut output mainly because electricity demand fell
questions.explain: ¶2: กำลังผลิตเพิ่มขึ้นมหาศาลใน “roughly two years” แต่ “Transmission lines in the sunniest provinces could not carry all the electricity being produced” แสดงว่าสายส่งขยายตามไม่ทัน ตัวเลือก D ผิดเพราะต้นเหตุคือความจุของสายส่ง ไม่ใช่ความต้องการไฟฟ้าลดลง และ C ขัดกับ “the losses were considerable”

questions.q: The phrase 'these sites' in paragraph 3 refers to
options: inland areas with low average wind speeds
specialised ports used to install turbines
waters off Vietnam and the Philippines
the few favourable onshore locations
questions.explain: ประโยคก่อนหน้าใน ¶3 คือ “Offshore, however, conditions are considerably better, particularly along the coasts of Vietnam and the Philippines” ดังนั้น ‘these sites’ คือพื้นที่นอกชายฝั่งของสองประเทศนี้ ตัวเลือก D ผิดเพราะทำเลบนบกถูกกล่าวถึงในฐานะที่มีศักยภาพจำกัด ไม่ใช่สิ่งที่กำลังพัฒนาอย่างยากลำบาก

questions.q: The word 'intermittent' in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to
options: independent
irregular
costly
remote
questions.explain: ‘intermittent’ = ไม่ต่อเนื่อง/เกิดเป็นช่วง ๆ ¶4: grids were not designed “to balance thousands of small and intermittent generators” ซึ่งสอดคล้องกับประโยคก่อนหน้าว่าไฟฟ้าจากแสงอาทิตย์หายไปทุกเย็นและลมอาจหยุดได้หลายวัน ตัวเลือก A เป็นกับดักเพราะผู้ผลิตรายเล็กอาจเป็นอิสระก็จริง แต่ไม่ใช่ความหมายของคำนี้

questions.q: According to paragraph 4, how do pumped hydro schemes help to balance supply and demand?
options: by sending surplus hydropower from Laos to neighbouring countries
by replacing large battery installations that have become too costly
by moving electricity quickly from one part of the grid to another
by using spare power to pump water uphill for later release
questions.explain: ¶4: pumped hydro schemes “use surplus electricity to pump water uphill for release when demand rises” ตัวเลือก A คือการค้าข้ามพรมแดน (แนวทางที่สอง) และ C คือการเสริมระบบสายส่ง (แนวทางแรก) ไม่ใช่การกักเก็บพลังงาน ส่วน B ขัดกับข้อความว่าแบตเตอรี่ “have become much cheaper”

questions.q: Which of the following best expresses the meaning of this sentence from paragraph 5: 'As a result, an identical solar farm may produce considerably more expensive electricity in Manila or Jakarta than in Madrid'?
options: Higher financing costs make the same solar project's power dearer in poorer economies.
Solar farms in Manila and Jakarta produce less power because they receive less sunshine overall.
Electricity prices in Europe are rising more slowly than those in Southeast Asian cities.
Investors prefer Madrid because the solar technology available there is more advanced.
questions.explain: ¶5: ประโยคนี้เป็นผลต่อเนื่องจากประโยคก่อนหน้าที่ว่าความเสี่ยง “push this cost to two or three times the level in wealthy countries” คือต้นทุนทางการเงินสูงกว่า โครงการเดียวกันจึงให้ไฟฟ้าราคาแพงกว่า ตัวเลือก B ผิดเพราะบทความไม่ได้พูดถึงปริมาณแสงแดดของเมืองเหล่านี้ และเทคโนโลยีใน D ก็เหมือนกันทุกประการ (identical)

questions.q: The word 'those' in paragraph 6 refers to
options: long-term contracts
coal-fired plants
electricity utilities
international lenders
questions.explain: ¶6: “Unlike those in Europe or North America, many of these plants are less than fifteen years old” — ‘those’ คือโรงไฟฟ้าถ่านหินในยุโรปและอเมริกาเหนือ ซึ่งผู้เขียนนำมาเทียบอายุกับโรงไฟฟ้าในภูมิภาคที่ยังใหม่กว่ามาก ตัวเลือก A ผิดเพราะสัญญาระยะยาวถูกกล่าวถึงในประโยคถัดไป

questions.q: Why does the author mention coal-mining districts in Indonesia in paragraph 7?
options: to show that coal mining is no longer profitable anywhere in the region
to suggest that new solar farms should be built on former mining land
to contrast Indonesia's energy policy with the approach taken by Vietnam
to illustrate how communities may suffer if fossil-fuel jobs disappear
questions.explain: ¶7: เขตเหมืองถ่านหิน “depend heavily on the industry for jobs and local government revenue” การปิดเหมืองโดยไม่มีทางเลือกจึงจะกระทบชุมชนและถูกต่อต้าน เป็นตัวอย่างประกอบหลัก just transition ตัวเลือก A ผิดเพราะบทความไม่ได้พูดถึงผลกำไรของเหมืองเลย

questions.q: Which of the following statements is an opinion rather than a fact?
options: Indonesia and Vietnam agreed energy transition partnerships in 2022.
Many of the region's coal plants are less than fifteen years old.
Consultation and retraining are essential conditions for success.
Laos already exports some of its hydropower to neighbouring countries.
questions.explain: ¶7: สิ่งเหล่านี้ “are therefore not optional extras but conditions for success” เป็นการประเมินของผู้เขียนว่าอะไร ‘จำเป็น’ จึงเป็นความคิดเห็น ส่วน A, B และ D เป็นข้อมูลที่ตรวจสอบได้ (ปีที่ทำข้อตกลง อายุโรงไฟฟ้า และการส่งออกไฟฟ้าของลาว)

questions.q: The author's overall attitude toward the future of renewable energy in Southeast Asia is best described as
options: cautiously hopeful
deeply pessimistic
uncritically enthusiastic
entirely indifferent
questions.explain: ¶8: ผู้เขียนเห็นว่าภูมิภาคมี “a genuine opportunity” (มีความหวัง) แต่ย้ำว่าจะสำเร็จหรือไม่ขึ้นกับการตัดสินใจทางการเมือง (มีเงื่อนไข) จึงเป็นการมองบวกอย่างระมัดระวัง ไม่ใช่ uncritically enthusiastic (C) เพราะบทความใช้พื้นที่ส่วนใหญ่อธิบายอุปสรรค

questions.q: What name is given to guaranteed prices paid for every unit of electricity fed into the grid? (Answer in NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage.)
questions.explain: ¶2: “generous feed-in tariffs — guaranteed prices paid for every unit of electricity fed into the grid” — ข้อความหลังขีดยาวคือคำนิยามของคำตอบ ซึ่งเป็นแรงจูงใจที่ทำให้โซลาร์ในเวียดนามเติบโตอย่างรวดเร็ว

questions.q: Which word in paragraph 2 refers to an instruction telling power plants to reduce their output? (Answer in ONE WORD from the passage.)
questions.explain: ¶2: “grid operators were forced to order curtailment, instructing plants to reduce output even when the sun was shining” — คือการสั่งให้โรงไฟฟ้าลดกำลังผลิตแม้จะผลิตได้

questions.q: What extreme weather events must offshore turbines in the region be engineered to survive? (Answer in ONE WORD from the passage.)
questions.explain: ¶3: “Turbines must be engineered to survive typhoons” — เป็นหนึ่งในสามความท้าทายของพลังงานลมนอกชายฝั่ง ร่วมกับท่าเรือ/เรือเฉพาะทางและระยะเวลาพัฒนาโครงการที่ยาวนาน

questions.q: What term refers to the interest rates and returns that lenders and investors demand? (Answer in NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage.)
questions.explain: ¶5: “the cost of capital — the interest rates and returns that lenders and investors demand” — โครงการพลังงานหมุนเวียนอ่อนไหวต่อค่านี้มากเพราะต้นทุนเกือบทั้งหมดเกิดตอนก่อสร้าง

questions.q: What are investments that lose their value before the end of their expected lifetimes called? (Answer in NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage.)
questions.explain: ¶6: “Retiring the plants early would turn them into stranded assets — investments that lose their value before the end of their expected lifetimes” — นี่คือเหตุผลที่การปลดระวางโรงไฟฟ้าถ่านหินอายุน้อยมีต้นทุนสูง
